major_concerns: Verifier/emulator semantic mismatch (vendor CLI coverage may be incomplete) leading to false-accepts/false-rejects.
Repair loop may overfit to verifier rules (satisfy verifier but fail dynamic semantics).
Emulator (Mininet/Kathará) may not capture stateful/vendor-specific behaviors used in production.
Risk of model/API rate limits or transient failures biasing outcomes if not strictly controlled.
required_design_repairs: Validate verifier coverage against a gold-labelled subset (human-reviewed or device-executed) and report false-accept/false-reject rates.
Include conservative and permissive verifier rule-sets and report sensitivity analyses.
Provide concrete anti-overfitting safeguards for repair loop (e.g., diversity-promoting objectives, verifier+emulator checks) and log repair transcripts.
Predefine retry policy and model-call budget; instrument and report API failures and their handling.

major_concerns: Legal/privacy restrictions may prevent inclusion of representative real vendor configs; synthetic/sanitized data may not fully reflect production.
Scope/scale risk: dataset+emulator+evaluation release is large and may exceed a short five-page presentation unless focused.
Emulator limitations may bias conclusions about real-device behavior.
Curation choices can introduce evaluation bias favoring some pipelines.
required_design_repairs: Define and document a reproducible data-generation/sanitization pipeline and provenance metadata; publish licensing and redaction policies.
Constrain the paper to a core reproducible subset (e.g., 100–200 canonical tasks) for the five-page submission and describe broader release plan.
Provide validation comparing emulator outcomes to a small set of real-device or vendor-validated cases if possible.
Include explicit evaluation-harness and scripts, plus seed/config logs, to maximize reproducibility and reduce selection bias.

major_concerns: Attack generation may be model-specific; results might not generalize across LLM APIs.
Publishing attack details risks enabling misuse; ethical disclosure must be handled responsibly.
Mitigations tested may be ad hoc and not representative of stronger defenses.
Emulator-ground-truth limitations affect measured impact of attacks.
required_design_repairs: Preregister attacker threat model and ensure cross-model evaluation (at least two different LLM APIs) to assess generality.
Adopt a responsible-disclosure plan: publish high-level results and redacted attack artefacts, release mitigations but with cautionary notes.
Include sensitivity analyses showing which attacks transfer across models and which are model-specific.
Validate attack consequences against emulator+verifier and, where feasible, a small vetted real-device subset or expert review.

major_concerns: Simulated delegation as a 'perfect-correction' black box overstates real human operator behavior and may bias recommended thresholds.
Workload sampling choices and simulated latencies heavily influence Pareto frontiers; external validity is limited.
Latency estimates depend on real-world API/network variability not fully captured in simulation.
required_design_repairs: Replace or augment perfect-correction delegation with at least one imperfect/human-like correction model (latency/error distribution) and report sensitivity.
Provide multiple workload mixes and report how recommendations change; preregister workload sampling procedure.
Measure and report model-call latency variance (empirical API timing) and incorporate into latency estimates; present conservative operating points.
Clearly frame recommendations as simulation-derived and require site-specific validation before production use.
